datasets.title: Satellite detected water extent over Ferfer Woreda, Shabelle District, Shabelle Region, Ethiopia as of 30 March 2023
datasets.description: UNOSAT code FL20230327SOM This map illustrates satellite detected surface waters in Ferfer Woreda, Shabelle District, Shabelle Region, Ethiopia as observed from a SPOT-6 image acquired on 30 March 2023 at 07:01 UTC. Within the analyzed area of about 260km2, about 4 km2 of lands appear to be flooded. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/water-extent-over-ferfer-woreda-shabelle-district-shabelle-region-ethiopia-as-of-30-march-]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: SPOT-6 satellite imagery acquired on 30 March 2023 was analyzed by UNOSAT analysts through visual interpretation and comparison with reference imagery to detect surface water extent. The flooded area was delineated and quantified within the 260 km² study area of Ferfer Woreda, resulting in vector geodatabase and shapefile outputs with area measurements.

sources.name: United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT)
sources.description: Satellite imagery analysis using SPOT-6 sensor to detect and map surface water extent through visual interpretation and comparison of multi-temporal satellite images
